message:
Power-Systems Engineer:

Manager and Aero-Rotor Lead, the lower winding keeps light-wind production alive through regulation, not just at top wind. Plain words: the same slow spin now makes enough push to wake the regulator, so the tunnel load sees steady power from light to strong wind. Low regulated power is 2.08 W in the low-wind regulated power (E80) from 3.27 W shaft in the shaft power at 5 m/s (E11), while high regulated stays 22.1 W in the regulated load power (E66), with volts 8.41 V to 18.5 V in the required Kv revision (E76) inside 8 to 40 V in the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60), where Kv means speed per volt; like a night-light at light wind rising to laptop level at strong wind, which is ordinary.

Safety-Control Integrator, I confirm what you take from the Braking ideas for wind turbines (E42) that brakes are spring-applied fail-safe, which from power side means the dump grid is a slowing aid not a park means. Plain words: the resistor bites harder with higher volts to help slow, then goes limp at standstill so the spring must hold alone. Dump is 85.6 W in the revised dump power (E78) for seconds against 109 J spin in the spin-down energy (E47) with 4.35 K rise in the brake disc temperature (E53), about one household bulb flashing for a second, so heat is ordinary.

Structures-Survival Engineer, I take up the CWC 2019 Rules and Requirements Manual_20190104 (E41) which requires shutdown on command and on load disconnect, which from power side means raw Direct Current (DC), meaning current in one direction, must always have somewhere to go inside the body. Plain words: all wires stay inside the nose and down the post bore clear of the disc, switching between tunnel load and dump grid, so a lost load wire cannot leave volts stranded. This keeps the 8.41 V to 18.5 V path in the required Kv revision (E76) inside the body with no added push on your post.

Ready, because v2 with 170 to 180 Kv spans regulation from 2.08 W to 22.1 W with dump as slowing aid and spring doing parking, and remaining power-curve and timed-stop checks are named bench tests.
